observation.visible_scene: Close-up of a white plastic pump dispenser (ribbed collar, threaded shaft, lever nozzle) gripped from above by a hand's thumb and index finger, set against a blurred pale basin/sink background. A viscous, translucent-white liquid is present at the nozzle throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: At t=0.00–0.32 s a thin, nearly vertical thread of liquid hangs from the nozzle tip with little change.
Around t=0.40–0.48 s a rounded drop swells at the nozzle tip.
From t=0.56–0.64 s the drop elongates downward into a thicker falling strand that continues through t=0.72–1.12 s, with the strand's thickness fluctuating.
Around t=1.20–1.28 s a new drop bulges at the nozzle and again stretches into a downward strand (t=1.36–1.60 s).
By t=1.68–1.76 s the strand thins and largely breaks, leaving a short hanging thread.
From t=1.84–3.20 s the flow reduces to a thin, mostly steady vertical thread, with minor thickness wobbles near t=2.16–2.32 s.
The hand and pump head remain in roughly the same vertical position across the clip; any small up/down shift of the lever is slight and not clearly resolved.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the pump was pressed before t=0.00 s or released after t=3.20 s.
The identity of the liquid and where it lands (the stream exits the bottom of the frame).
What triggered the drop swellings (press vs. release of the pump).
uncertain_details: Camera motion: the background framing appears nearly static but a slight drift cannot be ruled out.
Whether the pump lever is actively depressed or held steady during the streaming phases.
Material/brand of the dispenser and exact fluid type.
